From Website to Release: What Eastar Map Has Prepared

Updated: 2026-09-21

← Back to documents

From brand entry and product description to application scenarios and a release path, this article reviews the foundation the Eastar Map website already provides.

BrandRelease readiness

For a product to reach users, a feature introduction is not enough. It needs a clear brand entry, product description, application scenarios, contact methods, and a release path. Judging from the current website output, Eastar Map has already built this foundation.

The home page states the brand

The home page places the Eastar Map positioning on the first screen: “Eastar Map builds on electronic charts and intelligent warning systems to provide safe, simple, efficient, and far-reaching support for every vessel.” This sentence states three things: the subject is navigation scenarios, the core capabilities are electronic charts and warning, and the goal is navigation support.

The product page states the capabilities

The product page is built around five capabilities:

  • Precise chart display
  • Real-time positioning and track
  • Intelligent risk warning
  • Efficient route planning
  • Multi-scenario fit

This content suits the website, and it can also be adapted into articles, product introduction visuals, and sales communication material.

The scenarios page states the use cases

The scenarios page places the product in ocean shipping, coastal fishing, inland waterways, port operations, maritime supervision, and yacht cruising. Compared with listing features alone, this makes it easier for users to understand who the system helps, with what, and in which situations.

The release entry is already in place

Both the home page and the product page carry a Release entry pointing to GitHub Releases, which shows that the material is not only for presentation but also reserves a place for future release and download entry. The current launch checklist also records QR codes, email, website, copyright, logo, release CTA, product screenshots, and English pages.

Eastar Map now has the basic content from brand presentation and product description to application scenarios and a release entry. The next step is to keep filling in real verification, user cases, and reusable release material.
